name: Chat transcript drives a UI tooltip walkthrough
looks: A chat panel types on the left: a short greeting, a user's question, then a reply with a one-line summary card. On the right, exactly as the reply names the action, a tooltip with a step counter lands on the matching button in a live product screen, a cursor moves to it and clicks, and the panel updates. A second question-and-reply beat repeats the move with a different part of the screen.
build: Fixed two-panel split (chat left, product UI right). Chat text types on 20-35ms per step; the reply's summary card rises in once the line finishes. The tooltip (arrow + short label + 'n of 4' badge) clips in next to the exact element the reply names, a cursor glyph tweens to it and does a quick click-scale, then that part of the UI updates. Only one tooltip is live at a time; the previous one clears before the next lands.
sound: A soft typewriter patter under the chat text, a light pop on each message landing, a distinct click exactly on the cursor's click.
prompt: Split the frame between a typed chat conversation and a live product screen. As each reply names a specific action, land a tooltip with a step counter on the exact matching UI element, move a cursor to it and click, and update that part of the screen right on that beat, so two or three exchanges visibly drive the interface instead of just narrating it.
